meta.title: TrekLink: LoRa mesh safety for routes with no signal
meta.description: TrekLink is a LoRa mesh that keeps a trekking group reachable where the cellular network stops, carrying position, status and SOS between handsets and syncing every event to basecamp when an uplink returns.

problem.heading: A multi-day route is a multi-day blackout
problem.lede: Vietnam's long trekking routes run through cellular dead zones that last for days, not minutes. The group is out of contact for the whole crossing, and so is anyone who would come for them.
problem.without.label: Without a mesh
problem.without.a: A fall is discovered when somebody walks back to find out why a person stopped.
problem.without.b: The guide cannot say where the group is, because nothing can carry the answer out.
problem.without.c: Basecamp learns what happened after the group returns, which is too late to act on.
problem.with.label: With TrekLink
problem.with.a: A fall raises an alarm on the carrier's own device, with a window to cancel it if the person is fine.
problem.with.b: Position and status hop between handsets, so the group tracks itself with no infrastructure.
problem.with.c: Basecamp receives the queued record of every event as soon as one node reaches an uplink.
nodes.heading: One node, three versions
nodes.lede: Every version runs the same TrekLink firmware over a LoRa mesh. They differ in the board they are built on and in how a carrier raises an SOS.
nodes.carousel.label: Node versions
node.v2.name: Node v2
node.v2.body: The development board version. A separate physical button does one thing, which is the right answer when the person pressing it is in trouble.
node.v2.alt: A TrekLink node version 2 on a workbench cutting mat, in its white boxed enclosure with an OLED display and a screw-on antenna.
node.v3.name: Node v3
node.v3.body: The carried version, on the T-Beam platform with GPS on board. SOS moves to a deliberate three-second hold on the general button, so a pocket cannot send one.
node.v3.alt: Placeholder for a photograph of TrekLink node version 3.
node.v4.name: Node v4
node.v4.body: The current version, on T-Beam Supreme. Same firmware, same gesture, more headroom for the fall detection and queueing work this project adds.
node.v4.alt: A TrekLink node version 4 held in one hand, in the slim ribbed enclosure, its OLED display lit and showing status.
research.heading: What this project is adding
research.lede: The mesh firmware already works and is not being rebuilt. The work is in what happens to an event between the moment a device raises it and the moment a responder sees it.
research.a.title: Nothing is lost while the link is down
research.a.body: An event raised in a dead zone is held on the device itself and delivered in order once a link returns, rather than existing only in the moment it was sent.
research.b.title: Basecamp is part of the path
research.b.body: The bridge between the mesh and the cloud sits at basecamp rather than being carried, because the person on the route carries a node and not a laptop.
research.c.title: A fall is a question before it is an alarm
research.c.body: Motion alone cannot tell a stumble from a fall, so the device asks first and gives the carrier a window to answer before anything leaves the node.
research.d.title: An alarm that arrived stays arrived
research.d.body: Once a broadcast has gone out, silencing the buzzer on the handset does not retract it. The platform keeps the incident open until a responder closes it.
